//: Compiler settings for the serverless functions.
The root tsconfig.json is a solution file — `files: []` plus references — so
it carries no compilerOptions at all. The platform compiles api/*.ts with the
nearest tsconfig it can find, which meant bare TypeScript defaults: ES5 output,
classic module resolution, no ESM interop. A function with no relative imports
survives that; one that imports across directories does not, and fails at
runtime as an opaque 500 with no body.
This file is what the function build should have been using all along.
NodeNext is deliberate: it is what the platform actually runs, and it makes
the compiler reject the extensionless relative imports that Node's ESM
resolver cannot follow. That exact mistake took down the generation route
with an unreadable 500 — the compiler now catches it instead.
